issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and timeliness
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction and that the notice of appeal and post-trial filings were timely.

issues.label: Preservation of speedy-trial claim
issues.why: The court must determine whether the constitutional speedy-trial claim was properly raised, litigated, and preserved for review.

issues.label: Speedy-trial right attachment
issues.why: The court must decide when the Sixth Amendment speedy-trial right attached (e.g., arrest/indictment) versus pre-accusation delay rules.

issues.label: Pre-indictment delay due process
issues.why: If delay occurred before accusation, the court must consider whether due process limits were violated by prejudicial, intentional delay.

issues.label: Length of delay threshold
issues.why: The court must determine the total relevant delay and whether it is presumptively prejudicial to trigger full Barker analysis.

issues.label: Delay calculation start point
issues.why: The court must select the correct start date for measuring delay (indictment vs arrest vs earlier accusation).

issues.label: Delay calculation end point
issues.why: The court must determine the proper endpoint (trial start) for measuring constitutional delay.

issues.label: Reasons for delay allocation
issues.why: The court must parse reasons for each period of delay and attribute them to the State, the defense, or neutral causes.

issues.label: Investigative delay justification
issues.why: The court must assess whether the long investigation before arrest/indictment is a valid reason or governed by different standards.

issues.label: Negligence vs bad faith
issues.why: The court must classify any State-caused delay as negligent, administrative, or deliberate to weight it properly.

issues.label: Defense-caused continuances
issues.why: The court must account for any continuances, motions, or strategy choices attributable to Sheffield that toll or weigh against him.

issues.label: COVID or systemic delays
issues.why: The court must consider whether court-system disruptions are neutral reasons and how they weigh in the balance.

issues.label: Assertion of right timing
issues.why: The court must evaluate when and how strongly Sheffield asserted a speedy-trial right and the weight to give it.

issues.label: Demand for speedy trial specificity
issues.why: The court must decide whether Sheffield’s filings constituted a clear demand for speedy trial versus a dismissal-only motion.

issues.label: Prejudice—oppressive incarceration
issues.why: The court must determine whether pretrial incarceration occurred and whether it was oppressive under Barker.

issues.label: Prejudice—anxiety and concern
issues.why: The court must assess evidence of particularized anxiety or reputational harm caused by the delay.

issues.label: Prejudice—defense impairment
issues.why: The court must decide whether the delay impaired the defense via lost evidence, faded memories, unavailable witnesses, or compromised testing.

issues.label: Presumed prejudice applicability
issues.why: The court must consider whether the delay is so long or State fault so weighty that prejudice is presumed.

issues.label: Causation of claimed prejudice
issues.why: The court must link any claimed prejudice to the delay rather than to ordinary trial difficulties or other causes.

issues.label: Barker balancing ultimate call
issues.why: The court must weigh all Barker factors together to decide whether dismissal is constitutionally required.

issues.label: State constitutional speedy-trial
issues.why: The court must determine whether any state constitutional speedy-trial protections apply differently than the federal standard.

issues.label: Statutory speedy-trial provisions
issues.why: The court must consider whether any statutory speedy-trial rights were invoked and, if so, whether their requirements were met.

issues.label: Standard of review—speedy trial
issues.why: The court must apply the correct appellate standard (legal conclusions de novo, factual findings for clear error/deference).

issues.label: Factual findings adequacy
issues.why: The court must ensure the trial court made sufficient findings to permit meaningful review of the speedy-trial ruling.

issues.label: Remedy for speedy-trial violation
issues.why: If a violation is found, the court must apply the correct remedy—dismissal with prejudice of the prosecution.

issues.label: Sufficiency standard (Jackson)
issues.why: The court must apply the Jackson v. Virginia standard viewing evidence in the light most favorable to the verdict.

issues.label: Elements of malice murder
issues.why: The court must ensure evidence supports each element, including intent to kill and malice aforethought.

issues.label: Proof of identity as shooter
issues.why: The court must decide whether circumstantial and direct evidence allows a rational juror to find Sheffield was the killer.

issues.label: Circumstantial evidence rule
issues.why: If the case is wholly circumstantial, the court must consider any applicable rule requiring exclusion of reasonable hypotheses.

issues.label: Reasonable alternative hypothesis
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the burglary theory is a reasonable hypothesis that the evidence fails to exclude.

issues.label: Motive evidence relevance
issues.why: The court must decide how motive evidence (affair/relationship) supports intent and identity without substituting for proof.

issues.label: Admissibility of affair evidence
issues.why: The court must consider whether evidence about Stephens was properly admitted (relevance, prejudice, character limits).

issues.label: Other-acts/character evidence limits
issues.why: The court must assess whether any evidence functioned as improper propensity evidence and whether limiting instructions were required.

issues.label: Cell phone/photos authentication
issues.why: The court must ensure proper foundation and authentication for the phone and photographs admitted into evidence.

issues.label: Stipulation effect on proof
issues.why: The court must determine how the parties’ stipulation about phone nonuse affects permissible inferences and sufficiency.

issues.label: Fire/accelerant inference limits
issues.why: The court must assess whether expert testimony about unusual fire behavior supports arson/cover-up inferences reliably.

issues.label: Expert testimony reliability
issues.why: The court must consider whether expert opinions (fire, medical examiner) met admissibility standards and were properly applied.

issues.label: Cause and manner of death
issues.why: The court must confirm medical evidence supports death by shooting before fire and the implications for malice and cover-up.

issues.label: Shotgun evidence linkage
issues.why: The court must decide whether recovery of a burned shotgun component supports inference of murder weapon and defendant access.

issues.label: Missing weapons inference
issues.why: The court must consider what inferences are permissible from the missing .32 weapon and displaced gun safe.

issues.label: Evidence of staging/cover-up
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether fire setting and body location support consciousness of guilt versus alternative explanations.

issues.label: Timeline opportunity evidence
issues.why: The court must assess whether the timing of Edith’s arrival, fire discovery, and Sheffield’s movements support opportunity.

issues.label: Defendant conduct post-fire
issues.why: The court must decide what weight to give to Sheffield’s demeanor, lack of inquiry, and focus on property as consciousness of guilt.

issues.label: Third-party access and scene security
issues.why: The court must consider evidence of multiple bystanders and woods activity and whether it undermines identity proof.

issues.label: Physical evidence chain of custody
issues.why: The court must ensure critical items (shotgun parts, body-related evidence, phone) had adequate chain-of-custody support.

issues.label: Jury credibility determinations
issues.why: The court must respect the jury’s role in weighing credibility (e.g., Stephens, neighbors) while assessing legal sufficiency.

issues.label: Inferences from jewelry/purse intact
issues.why: The court must assess whether lack of theft undermines burglary hypothesis and supports domestic motive without overreach.

issues.label: Plastic straws in hand meaning
issues.why: The court must consider whether this evidence supports any inference (struggle/defense/scene) and whether speculation occurred.

issues.label: Harmless-error framework
issues.why: For any non-structural trial error raised, the court must decide whether it was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt or under state standards.

issues.label: Cumulative error possibility
issues.why: If multiple errors are found, the court must consider whether their cumulative effect warrants a new trial.

issues.label: New trial motion standards
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standards governing denial of a motion for new trial and deference to trial court findings.

issues.label: Evidentiary hearing fairness
issues.why: The court must consider whether post-trial evidentiary hearings were properly conducted and rulings supported by the record.

issues.label: Sufficiency vs weight distinction
issues.why: The court must ensure Sheffield’s challenge is treated as legal sufficiency rather than reweighing evidence.
